sourceNote: Selective DGT editorial notes for Jude.

1:5: SBLGNT reads “Jesus” (Ἰησοῦς) as the one who saved a people out of Egypt. This is a well-known textual variant; some manuscripts read “Lord.” DGT follows its displayed SBLGNT base text.
1:9: Jude refers to Michael’s dispute with the devil over Moses’ body, a tradition not narrated in the Old Testament. The verse itself does not identify its literary source.
1:12: σπιλάδες can denote hidden reefs and, in related usage, spots or blemishes. DGT uses “hidden reefs,” fitting Jude’s sequence of vivid danger images.
1:14: Jude’s wording here closely corresponds to 1 Enoch 1:9. DGT translates Jude’s Greek directly rather than importing wording from an English translation of 1 Enoch.
1:22: Jude 22–23 has unusually complex manuscript variation involving the sequence and wording of the three groups. DGT follows the displayed SBLGNT text, which gives: show mercy to those who doubt; save others from the fire; show mercy to others with fear.
1:25: “Before all time” renders πρὸ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος, followed by “now” and “into all the ages,” an unusually expansive temporal doxology.
